sentences.text: The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Tarlok Singh Chauhan, Acting Chief Justice.
The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Satyen Vaidya, Judge.
Whether approved for reporting?

No. For the
Applicants/ Appellants: Mr. Anup Rattan, A.G. with Mr. Rakesh Dhaulta, Mr. Pranay Pratap Singh,
Mr. Govind Korla, Addl. A.Gs. and Ms. Priyanka Chauhan and Mr. Arsh Rattan, Dy. A.Gs.
For the Respondents: Mr. Jangan Nath, Advocate. Tarlok Singh Chauhan, Acj (Oral)
By medium of this application, the applicants/appellants have sought condonation of 176 days' delay that has crept-up in filing of the appeal.

Even though this application is vehemently opposed by learned counsel for the respondents, however, for the reasons as set out in the application, more particularly, paras 2(c) and 2(d) thereof, which are duly supported by the affidavit of the concerned Superintending Engineer, we deem it appropriate to condone 2024:HHC:11410 the aforesaid delay.
Ordered accordingly.
The application stands disposed of.
Appeal be registered.

2. The land of the respondents had been utilized by the appellants-State for the construction of Dehar to Triphalghat road without acquiring the same and without paying any compensation to the respondents.
3. Therefore, the respondents approached this Court and sought direction to the appellants-State to acquire their land and pay compensation to them in accordance with law in a time bound manner.

Date Of Decision: 12.11.2024 vs Lekh Ram & Ors on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112124027/
1 4.

The appellants-State sought to oppose the grant of relief to the respondents on the ground of delay and latches, and also on the pretext that while the road was being constructed, the respondents had not raised any objection, but had voluntarily donated the land for construction of the road.

5. The learned Writ Court rejected the contention of the appellants-State by placing reliance on a detailed judgment of the learned Coordinate Bench of this Court in CWP No. 2948 of 2023, titled as Manbhari & Ors. vs. State of H.P. & Ors., decided on 19.09.2023, wherein after placing reliance on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme 2024:HHC:11410 Court in Vidya Devi vs. State of Himachal Pradesh and others (2020) 2 SCC 569 and Sukh Dutt Ratra vs. State of Himachal Pradesh & others (2022) 7 SCC 508, held that the plea of delay and laches cannot be raised in the case of a continuing cause of action, especially in land acquisition matters, where acts of the State shock the conscience of the Court; and that too forcibly dispossess a person of his private property without following due process of law, would be violative of a "Human Right" and also a "Constitutional Right"
under Article 300A of the Constitution of India; and the plea of oral consent to the acquisition has no legal sanctity and cannot be countenanced.
7.

sentences.text: We completely agree with the reasoning of the learned Writ Court in the impugned judgment and find no merit in this appeal and the same is accordingly dismissed.
No costs.
